messages:
emily (support): Hey team, just escalated a customer case from ACME. Streaming SSE session gets a 429 mid-stream and client sees partial output. Customer insists they have quota. They sent logs and a short repro.
ryan (support): Copy. They say it happens about ~30% of streams, mostly long responses 1k+ tokens. Sometimes reconnect resumes and sometimes it restarts and duplicates.
emily (support): Key parts from the customer: their app opens /v1/streams?model=text-gen, sends Authorization: Bearer <api_key>, receives chunks for ~12s then a 429 JSON frame and connection close. They included this snippet:

```
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
content-type: text/event-stream

data: {"delta":"..."}
data: {"delta":"..."}
data: {"error":{"type":"rate_limit","message":"quota exceeded"}}
```

and curl output: `curl -H "Authorization: Bearer X" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/streams -N` -> 200 then 429 mid-stream.
rohan (eng): Hmm. Does the 429 come as an HTTP response or an SSE data event? In our stack we do both: we try to emit an event describing error then close with HTTP 200+stream end if streaming protocol allows. Need exact logs.
emily (support): Customer supplied server logs with request id `req_0a9c`. They show this around the end:

```
[2026-02-28T14:23:12Z] req_0a9c stream_start user=acct_234 token_id=tok_abc
[2026-02-28T14:23:22Z] auth.rotate token_id=tok_abc -> tok_def user=acct_234
[2026-02-28T14:23:24Z] stream_chunk req=0a9c tok=tok_def tokens_emitted=512
[2026-02-28T14:23:25Z] quota.check user=acct_234 tokens_remaining=0 -> reject
[2026-02-28T14:23:25Z] stream_error req=0a9c err=rate_limit
[2026-02-28T14:23:25Z] stream_close code=1006
```

jen (eng-sre): That looks like token rotation happened during the stream. We currently attribute quota to token IDs independently for short windows, and rotation can cause the accounting to look like a different token used, and then the ledger sees 0 remaining on the new token. Might be a race where billing counter isn't charged until end-of-stream, so interim checks fail.
rohan (eng): Repro plan: try to reproduce by simulating token rotation mid-stream + concurrent token buckets. I can spin up a local client that emits long streaming prompts and rotate the API key via our auth service.

Actionable repro steps for eng (from customer):
1) Start SSE: `curl -H "Authorization: Bearer tok_old" \ \ 
  "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/streams?model=long-gen" -N`
2) After 10s use internal auth API to rotate token: `POST /internal/rotate?user=acct_234` -> issues `tok_new`.
3) Observe server logs for `auth.rotate` and whether subsequent chunk frames are billed to tok_new; check for a 429 event mid-stream.

mateo (billing): If true, that could cause tokens to be double-counted or missed. We need to see ledger entries. Can we pull billing ledger for acct_234 for that window? I'll join.
ops-bot: Fetching logs: /logs/streams/req_0a9c -> https://internal-logs/redwood/streams/req_0a9c (private link)
rohan (eng): I ran a quick local sim and saw the same pattern: rotate -> subsequent chunks associated with new token -> quota check fails because new token had zero allowance in the token-bucket. I think two issues:
- We do token-bucket checks on each chunk against the active token record (which can change mid-stream).
- We defer actual billing ledger writes until stream end, so the allowance on the current token doesn't include in-flight usage.

jen (eng-sre): Short-term mitigation: treat a streaming session as anchored to the token that started it for quota checks, ignoring mid-stream rotation for enforcement. Long-term: change accounting so each chunk increments an in-memory in-flight counter tied to the session id (req_0a9c) and decrement on finalization/rollback, plus reconcile job to flush to ledger periodically.
emily (support): Customer asked for workaround now. Suggested: don't rotate tokens while active streams are open; or create longer-lived keys for streaming clients. They are asking for a hotfix.
rohan (eng): I don't love telling customers to avoid rotation but we can quickly add a gate: if auth.rotate occurs and session still active, copy allowance from old token to new token or mark new token as allowed for X remaining tokens = remaining of previous token. That would be a small change in auth service.
jen (eng-sre): Also need to ensure 429s are surfaced as SSE error events rather than raw HTTP 429, and include `Retry-After` header and `x-request-id` so clients can resume or correlate. Right now client sees ambiguous close.
ryan (support): Customer impact: they reported 6 incidents in last 48h, multiple duplicates in app state. They want a replay/duplication safe resume behavior. Can we provide an idempotency/resume token in the stream response so clients can request continuation instead of restart?
rohan (eng): We can add a resume token in initial handshake: `session_id` returned in the first SSE event. Client can request `?resume=session_id&cursor=tok_pos` to continue. But that's medium-term.

Action items:
- rohan: implement short-term auth gate to carry allowance across rotation for active sessions (P0 for support escalations). ETA 48h.
- jen: implement in-memory inflight counters + reconcile job design doc. ETA end of sprint.
- mateo: pull billing ledger and confirm no double-charge for affected periods; confirm whether any customers billed incorrectly. ETA 24h.
- emily/ryan: communicate mitigations and recommended workarounds to ACME, offer to monitor.

mateo (billing): FYI ledger snapshot for acct_234 shows charges aligning with emitted tokens, no duplicate billing yet — looks like we undercounted on token_id=tok_def because the ledger write didn't attribute in-flight tokens. We'll confirm.

emily (support): I'll draft message to ACME: explain root cause (token rotation + per-token quota enforcement + deferred ledger writes), give workaround (avoid rotation, use longer-lived streaming key), and timeline for hotfix and follow-ups.

rohan (eng): I'll open a PR for the auth gate and a short integration test reproducing rotation mid-stream. Adding `--flaky` test to our e2e streaming harness.

jen (eng-sre): Also adding improved logs: include `session_anchor_token` in stream logs so we can quickly map chunks to original token.

emily (support): Thanks team. Setting this thread P0 and tagging customer for a sync in 2 hours. :hourglass_flowing_sand:
